observations.detail: X-a18-stats-1 is presented as a SPEC violation, but the cited SPEC text does not say what the report claims. SPEC §4 says stats exists 'so ... any member can see the AGGREGATE'. That states a purpose. It does not say stats may hold only aggregates. The same section makes app/src/types.ts 'the typed source of truth', and ViewStats declares lastViewedByEmail?: string. SPEC §17 also endorses the same per-person shape on the same member-readable map: lastEditedByEmail 'is now the whole of the answer'. SPEC §17's 'Gated to isDocEditor' covers the activity panel, not docs/{id}. Under the plan's verdict codes this is a Q (SPEC question: report and ask), not a confirmed defect. Fix: retag it as a SPEC question for the user, and put types.ts:155 and the lastEditedByEmail precedent in its 'violates' text. Until the user rules, do not present it as a confirmed defect.

observations.detail: A18.1 asserts that the field X-a18-stats-1 calls a defect is present: the final stats must deepEqual {..., lastViewedByEmail: email}. So the unit requires the field to be there (A18.1 PASS) and to be absent (the TODO). If the product is fixed the way mutant m7 models it (the field removed), A18.1 turns red. m7 was only run against the TODO case, so this was never noticed. Fix: drop lastViewedByEmail from A18.1's oracle, or check it only through the editor-gated surface. Re-run m7's fix effect against A18.1 to confirm it stays green.

observations.detail: The catalogue's own oracle for 18.3 is 'MCP: apiReads +1 only, with ms:0', and it has never been seen red. controls-a18-automated-reads patches only recordView (isAutomated && false). The MCP path writes through recordApiRead (functions/src/mcp/tools.ts:397-426), which the patch leaves alone. The control's RED message comes from the cli POST /view assertion at line 375. To get there, the MCP loop (lines 354-368) must have passed with the patch applied, so its assertions were green throughout. No spec mutation covers them either. Fix: add a patch set, e.g. recordApiRead incrementing stats.views or writing ms > 0, expecting 'get_document #1 moved no human number' or 'an automated session with ms 0'. Alternatively, record a spec mutation that plants the bug.

observations.detail: SPEC §17 says the panel 'shows both and filters to human-only or automation-only'. The case only asserts rows.some(badge 'via cli') and rows.some(badge 'via mcp') under Automation. That still passes if the filter does nothing (Everything == Automation). People is never clicked, and no row without a badge is shown to be excluded. The 'automated reads' tile is never compared with stats.apiReads, so 'shows both' is unchecked too. The owner's own browser session registers nondeterministically, OPEN_DELAY_MS after u.open, so the case has no reliable human row to exclude. Fix: before opening the panel, plant a human session with owner.http (POST /view 0, then 1200). Then assert: Automation rows all carry a badge and include no human row; People rows carry no badge and include the human row; the 'automated reads' tile equals stats.apiReads. Put these in a case without the defect tag (or in A18.4 proper), so X-a18-stats-3 does not hide them. They pass today with the cli row.

observations.detail: readInBrowser waits for stats.totalMs > 0 after leaving and treats that as 'pagehide sends the final beat'. The app also sends an interval beat every BEAT_MS = 60 s. The registration wait allows up to SETTLE_MS = 120 s, and the spec's own comment says a beat has taken 20 s under load. On a loaded stack an interval beat can therefore satisfy the wait before the pagehide beacon lands. Two results: (a) the final beat on leaving is not what gets measured; (b) visit.final (line 220) and the session read (line 221) can fall on either side of the late beacon, so S.ms != final.totalMs and the case gives a false FAIL at 253 or 309. This is a latent flake that the fresh-stack 3/3 does not exercise. Fix: after leaving, wait for the session and stats to agree and stay stable (eventually with stableSamples: stats.totalMs === views/{sid}.ms and lastBeatAt after the leave). Read both inside that wait.

observations.detail: recordView treats ms as an absolute total: 'a retried, duplicated or reordered beat is a no-op'. That is a separate invariant from the per-beat clamp. The case checks it at lines 699-703 (a lower, negative, non-numeric or duplicate claim leaves the session at MAX_BEAT_MS and does not move stats). It has never been seen red. controls-a18-beat-clamp fails at line 696, before these lines run, and no spec mutation targets them. Fix: add a patch that keeps line 696 green and breaks 699-703. For example, delta = Math.min(Math.abs(claimedMs - storedMs), MAX_BEAT_MS): the 1000 ms claim then adds 299 s. Or read a string ms with Number(). Expect 'a lower (reordered) claim leaves the session at 300000'.

observations.detail: The case can only turn green under one kind of fix: one that takes the format from somewhere other than the version record. Under the most direct fix for useDocument.ts:241's `?? "html"` fallback it FAILS instead. That fix holds Edit, or the Formatting toolbar, until the version record has loaded. enterEdit's click waits up to Playwright's 30 s action timeout and its toolbar wait up to 45 s (browser.mjs:2904-2907), but holdListen is capped at VERSION_READ_DELAY_MS = 8 s and releases on its own. So by the time the first palette is read, gate.records[0].releasedAt is set and `precondition(stillHeld, …)` throws E2E_PRECONDITION: a FAIL, never a PASS, against the fix protocol's 'the defect's e2e case turns green and stays as a regression test'. The unit's own proof that the oracle can pass, m-a101b-green, had to delete that precondition to pass. Fix: hold until the case releases it (ms null, under the case's own deadline). Accept 'Edit or the Formatting toolbar not offered while the read is held' as compliant: wait a bounded time for the toolbar, and if it is absent, release and assert that the first palette to appear is Markdown's. Keep only the 'read was held' precondition.

observations.detail: SPEC §11 makes md' === md'' a MUST for every Markdown document, and says the text of an author's <script>, <style> and <textarea> 'comes back byte for byte'. md' → html' → md'' is checked only on content/markdown-reference/bundle/index.md, which has a script but no <style>, no <textarea> and no comment beyond the leading SPDX line. Comment parking, style and textarea raw text, which are the most fragile serializer paths, are only ever checked on the first pass. A10.3's no-op commit cannot stand in for the second pass. While S8 holds, on stacks that enforce the RTDB rules and in production, that session adopts the stale live log and re-serialises the pre-commit DOM (the spec says so at :530-533), so its dedup is just a first pass run twice. On a stack without rtdb-rules (S31) the same session starts from html', so A10.3's dedup measures different things on different stacks and records neither. Fix: run A10.4's second-document pass on A10.3's v2 index.md as well (publish it as its own document, check its rendering equals v2's index.html, save it unchanged, compare the draft object with lineHunks). Alternatively, add PROBE_MD's style, textarea and mid-document comment blocks to A10.4's input.

observations.detail: Section wrapping is checked only as the list of `<section id="…">` ids in document order, by regex. SPEC §11 says each heading and its subordinate content is wrapped. Two broken renderings would pass. One is flat: every section is closed at the next heading whatever its level. The other emits an empty `<section id=x></section>` before each heading. The fixture has an h1 with two h2 under it, so structure is checkable. Parse v1 index.html (ctx.users.parser() or DOMParser) and assert three things: #notes and #notes-1 are children of #stored-twice; each heading section's first element child is its heading; #preamble comes before #stored-twice and is its sibling.

observations.detail: The 'zero external URLs' oracle (two doesNotMatch regexes) and the embedded-stylesheet match have never been seen red. The spec mutations cover only the zip (m-a102-zip) and the slugs (m-a102-slugs), and a negative regex is the kind of assertion that goes blind without anyone noticing. The attribute regex also misses some forms. I ran it in scratch: it does not match `srcset="<external-url>"`, `<object data="<external-url>">` or `<meta http-equiv=refresh content="0;url=<external-url>">`. Add a spec mutation that appends `<link rel=stylesheet href="<external-url>">` to `html` before the check, or a product control that puts one in render.ts's template, and see it go red. Better still, collect every attribute value and CSS url from a DOM parse instead of using a regex.

observations.detail: The check that presenting hides the banners and the comments panel passes when neither element exists. `hidden()` turns a missing element (null) into `false`, which is the same value as hidden, and the precondition only checks the header, toolbar and rail. On a fresh Q, `.viewer-banners` is not rendered (ViewerBanners.tsx:139 returns null when there are no rows, and Q has no scripts) and `.comments-panel` is not rendered either (useCommentsOpen keeps it collapsed until there is a thread; Sidebar renders only when showComments, DocViewer.tsx:1072). So the banners and comments parts of 'presenting hides the chrome' (both at :644 and in the refused-fullscreen step at :687) would still pass if viewer.css:321-322 were deleted. Fix: before presenting, give Q an open comment thread so the panel opens, and use a document that shows a banner (for example D untrusted, which shows 'scripts are blocked'). Add a precondition that both are displayed before Present. Also consider checking `.consent`, which viewer.css:323 hides too.

observations.detail: On the tall and short documents, the case checks only that `o` draws no overview and that ArrowDown does not page. It never checks whether the viewer left `o` alone, or whether a later Escape is left alone. Both sections are detected as slides (tall by rule 2, short by rule 5 with three id'd sections), so useDeck still binds its key handler: keysEnabled is not gated on isDeck, and the effect returns early only when slides.length is 0. The `o` branch (useDeck.ts:293-296) runs before the `paged` gate (:302), so it calls preventDefault on `o` and sets overviewOpen to true, while DocViewer hides the overview because hasSlides is false (:850, :1050). The next Escape then finds overviewOpenRef true and is also preventDefaulted (:286-289). That is a suspected breach of 'A document that is not a deck is unaffected' and of 'with the overview shut, Escape is left untouched', reached by reading the code and not yet run. Fix: in the tall and short loop, install installEscapeProbe plus a matching probe for `o`, press o and then Escape, and assert both were not defaultPrevented ([false]). If it fails, open a new X-a16-decks defect.

observations.detail: X-a16-decks-1's `violates` field cites SPEC §6d, but that sentence describes what the product does. SPEC says a stacked deck 'reads position from which slide is *shown* … with the deck's own attribute changes as the signal'. useDeck measures shownSlide on exactly that signal, a MutationObserver on class/style (useDeck.ts:174-188). At that moment the outgoing slide is the one shown by SPEC's own four properties. SPEC names no later signal, such as transitionend. So the defect stands on its concrete harm (every other ArrowRight is lost, and the rail marks the wrong slide on the repo's own sample), not on a broken SPEC sentence. Re-tag it as class I, or as P on concrete harm with a SPEC question attached. Its fix (for example, re-measuring after transitions, or not letting a mutation overwrite goTo's setCurrent) changes normative text, so it waits at G1. The failing assertion itself is correct: it is the defect's own oracle (:599), with the no-transitions twin as its precondition.

observations.detail: 'They go into the deck through its own keys' is only checked as `.active` moving and y staying 0. A product that toggled D's `.active` class itself would pass, and SPEC rules that out ('toggling the deck's class would style a document this app does not own'). The y:0 check is also vacuous on D, which cannot scroll (`.js body{overflow:hidden}`, `.deck{height:100vh}`). Fix: install a capture-phase keydown counter in D's unsandboxed frame and assert the number of untrusted ArrowRight/ArrowLeft events equals the distance moved. For example, a rail click from slide 2 to slide 5 should give 3 ArrowRight.

observations.detail: The report says S15 violates SPEC, but neither citation supports that. It rests on ADR 0014 ('limits a disabled account's remaining access to about an hour') and on SPEC §23's 'not disabled' check at refresh, and both cover OAuth grants (bsa_/bsr_) only. For personal tokens ADR 0014 Decision 3 says the opposite: 'The identity gate is re-checked at each refresh, which a personal token never gets.' SPEC §19's 'same identity, and therefore the same ACL' is about the ACL, not account state. So the behaviour S15 shows is documented: an I-class finding to ask about (the plan tags it Q), not a violation. The failing assertion is the right one; the classification and citation are wrong. Fix: rewrite product_suspicions.S15.violates and the spec header to cite ADR 0014:25-27 as acknowledging the behaviour, present 401 as the proposed answer to the question, and classify it I.

A2's parity matrix covers strangers, not a member who was just removed. Fix: keep the removed viewer's 404 response and assert its body bytes and Cache-Control equal the absent-id response's (Date aside), as a02-matrix-http does. Its RTDB mirror write is suspect S16: scripts/lib/firebase.mjs getApp calls initializeApp with no databaseURL (lines 95-99), and getRtdb returns null when admin.database() throws (lines 116-122). On production the precondition at spec:354 (`g.mirror?.ok`) will therefore FAIL the case, unclassified: README says precondition() FAILs. The case never reaches revocation, which is the part S16 actually breaks. The plan's production rule says to record the missing mirror and write it as presence.ts does, for run documents only. Fix: on production, write the mirror for the run document after recording the finding. Then let the RTDB revocation checks (spec:392-393, 400) be the oracle, under `defect: S16` scoped to prod, or end INCONCLUSIVE with the finding until S16 is settled.

observations.detail: The test cannot prove the CLI waits --interval between checks. (1) It passes `--interval 30`, so the SPEC floor ('at least 30', Math.max(MIN_INTERVAL_S, …)) is never exercised. (2) `r.ms >= 30_000` is timed from process start, not from the first check. On the shared stack one call takes 15-60 s (the spec's own header), so the first check plus the writer's comment already exceed 30 s, even for a CLI that re-checks every second. Fix: pass `--interval 1` (the floor makes it 30) and assert against the first check: `r.ms >= bg.firstCheckMs + 30_000 - slack`. Record when the comment's event landed, and end INCONCLUSIVE when it landed so late after the first check that the measurement cannot tell the two apart.

observations.detail: Three problems with the absence windows. (a) The window for 'no cover POST after a reload' starts at `tReload = Date.now()` after the reload has already resolved, so a POST sent before the load event is not counted. The editor's reload (lines 1174-1175) takes its mark before reloading, and this one should too. (b) Every posts:0 absence (the trusted deck, the control and the filed document at lines 1150-1152, and the reload) is judged after a fixed 6 s (BACKFILL_SETTLE_MS), counted from when the four owed covers are stored. The backfill handles one document at a time in updatedAt order, and the trusted deck may be the last one it looks at. Looking at it takes getEntry, a GET /content and, if the skip is broken, a capture, all under stack load, and 6 s does not bound that. So a broken trusted skip or a broken visibleDocs scope can send its POST after the window, and the case still passes. The control went red once on a fresh stack, which does not show it always will. Fix: before each settle, wait until the owner page's GET /content/<deckTrusted>/v1/<entry> has been answered (after the reload too). (c) Line 1171 counts the filed document's POSTs over the whole oWatch. A late POST sent while the document was off screen, followed by none inside the folder, still reads {posts:1}. Fix: count since the folder was opened, and assert 0 before that.

observations.detail: A20.4 asserts that 'every answer is private, no-store and exposes WWW-Authenticate', but its method matrix is POST, GET, DELETE and PUT only. It never sends the CORS preflight that a browser-hosted MCP client (the reason the expose header exists) sends before every Bearer POST, and no request carries an Origin header. The mcp function is onRequest({...PLAIN, cors: true}), and firebase-functions wraps the handler in cors({origin}). That middleware's default preflightContinue:false answers OPTIONS with 204 before the handler runs, so noStore (index.ts:3081) and the expose header (server.ts:205) are probably never set on a preflight. To fix: add OPTIONS /mcp with Origin, Access-Control-Request-Method: POST and Access-Control-Request-Headers: authorization,content-type, and record its status, cache-control, expose and ACAO in the same rows table. Also put a 400 (the text/plain -32700 from A20.3) and a 200 tools/call answer into those rows. If the preflight fails, this is likely a new TODO or an I-class SPEC §23 question rather than a P.

observations.detail: SPEC §6a requires the draft banner to say "who saved it last, and when". The spec checks who exactly, but DRAFT_BANNER makes the when optional: `( just now| \d+[mhd] ago)?`. observations.detail: The red depends on the harness reordering two requests from the same page. The redundant autosave was sent at +1003 ms. delayRequests' second rule held it until the commit had answered, and the commit was only sent at +1554 ms. So the server saw a request sent 551 ms earlier only after the later one was finished. The plan's bar for a P is that skeptics cannot show a harness artefact, and a reorder is the obvious attack. Production has a window that needs no reorder. commitDraft answers only after its transaction, then deleteFiles, then syncPublicProjection. DocViewer then awaits clearLog before setWantsEdit(false), and it is that effect cleanup which finally clears the debounce timer. A timer that fires in that window reaches a server where v2 is already current, and gets the 409 in send order. Re-force it that way: no hold on /draft; press Save inside the debounce; hold the /commit RESPONSE, after the server has handled it, until past the 1 s debounce (a lib request if delayRequests can only hold requests). Also add the positive control the plan asks for on expected-red suspects: in A9.8's main case, where the autosave finishes before Save, watch toasts for QUIET_MS after "Published v2." and assert no error.

observations.detail: The case reads meta (spec:720) and writes it to the evidence, but asserts only the toasts. POST /draft checks the base with a plain read. writeDraft then uploads the draft object and merge-sets `draft`, outside any transaction. So a redundant autosave that passes the check while the commit is uploading can bring back meta.draft {baseVersion:"v1"} and docs/<id>/draft/index.html after the commit's transaction and deleteFiles removed them. observations.detail: The S8 citation does not say what the report claims. SPEC §6b (spec.md:774-791) says nothing about the live log, and ADR 0010 never says the log wins over the draft. The normative sentence is in §22, spec.md:2531-2533: "Because the live log wins over the draft when an editor opens (§6b) … a log nobody is using is dropped with the write". ADR 0015 point 4 says the same. presence.ts:141 repeats the same wrong §6b reference. The concrete harm cited ("a v3 published from bytes after the commit … showed v2's text") is S8 combined with S6/S14: no path that publishes from bytes clears status/{doc}/y, because clearEditLog is called only from accept.ts. After an in-app commit on its own, the surviving log is the draft that just became v2, so an editor who adopts it sees v2. Either fix alone removes the cited harm: S8's, or the S14+S6 direction "every mint path … clears the live log", which the plan runs before S8. Fix: cite §22 (spec.md:2531-2533) and the intent at DocViewer.tsx:563-567. Then show a harm S8 causes on its own, or say plainly that the harm depends on S6/S14, so the fix order is judged on the right evidence. The oracle itself, y empty within 2 s of the toast, is fine.

observations.detail: No scenario declares inconclusiveOnStackTimeout, and none is wrapped in onAnsweringStack, so on a loaded shared stack Hosting's 60 s 504 and http.mjs's 60 s deadline both turn into plain FAILs. The run records class these FAILs as 'unclassified'. The report's prose says they are environment, but the results the harness keeps disagree. Fix: declare inconclusiveOnFunctionKill: true on every scenario. It implies inconclusiveOnStackTimeout, and every case settles events written by triggers. Also make the session clients with cutoffError: true. A21.5b also FAILs on its precondition whenever A21.5 failed, which adds one more unclassified FAIL each time. Let it stage its own one-publish document, or end INCONCLUSIVE when A21.5 did not run. Then a broken A21.5 no longer shows up as a second failure.

observations.detail: The case name claims pages are 'cut on (at, id)', but no two events share an `at`. Every event here is written by a trigger in its own commit, so the id half of the cut is never exercised. A product that paged with startAfter(at) alone would pass. Events written in one batch do share their serverTimestamp: POST /visibility writes doc.visibility and doc.expiry in one batch. To stage the tie: settle exactly 99 events (the publish plus 98 browser threads), then call setVisibility({visibility:'unlisted', expiresAt}). The tied pair then sits at positions 100 and 101. Assert that page 1 ends with one of the pair and page 2 starts with the other, each reported once (compareRecorded already orders by at, then id).

observations.detail: A second malformed shape is never probed. observations.detail: Only the input half and the one-second half of the arming rule are tested. The focus half never is. Phases 1–3 change only input and time, and the harness runs with focus emulation on, so the page always has focus. The product restarts its second on every blur, focus and visibilitychange event (Connect.tsx useArmed, where restart() runs only while document.hasFocus() is true and the page is visible). The rule exists to stop this attack: a page raises this window under the cursor between two clicks. A product that started the second at render and ignored focus would pass the whole case, and the consent-arm control (touched=true, 0 ms timer) cannot show otherwise. Add a phase: move the pointer from the start; about 800 ms after Approve appears, dispatch window 'blur' then 'focus' in the page. Then assert from the arming record that `enabled` comes at least 990 ms after that focus event. Add a control that drops the focus/blur listeners or the hasFocus() guard.

observations.detail: The case title says 'filing … send[s] nothing', but nothing files a document into a folder that already has a non-owner reader. The filed document is published at :305, before the folder is shared at :306, so filing grants nobody anything there. A product that emailed folder readers on publish-into-folder or on move would pass. After the folder grant, publish (or move_document) a second document into folderId. Then assert three things: iFolder is in that document's members, the shim's sends to iFolder are still only the folder invitation, and the final settleAll is unchanged.
observations.evidence: e2e/specs/functional/a23-email.spec.mjs:255 (title), 304-309 (newDoc with folderId runs before folderGrant). SPEC §13 (spec.md:1282-1284): 'Filing is sharing, and it is silent. A document filed into a folder is readable by everyone in the folder's members, and nobody is emailed: invitations go out only when sharing itself changes.' No other spec checks this with email on: A20.2.move_document is BOTH tier and reads no mail.

observations.detail: No case shows that a cooldown ever ends. No A23 case expects a second notice to the same (recipient, document, kind), so a cooldown that never expires would pass the whole unit. Examples are a COMMENT_EMAIL_COOLDOWN_MS in the wrong unit, or a window check that never reopens. The case is cheap on a LOCAL stack: with the admin SDK, backdate users/{O.uid}.emailCooldowns[d1] (and `${d1}:suggestions`) to more than 30 min ago. Then comment, and suggest, on d1. The owner must be told of each, and the key must be rewritten with a fresh time.
observations.evidence: e2e/specs/functional/a23-email.spec.mjs:617-648 (only 'inside the window' and 'different key' legs). The report's A23.4 note: 'The case never waits out the 30-minute cooldown'. SPEC §14 (spec.md:1357, 1368-1371): 'a per-(recipient, doc) cooldown' and '… is still one email per window'. functions/src/config.ts:32, functions/src/email/notify.ts:57-58.

observations.detail: timedOut() returns INCONCLUSIVE only when the shim saw no send to the refused recipient before the cut-off. Any refusal recorded before the cut-off FAILS the case, however late it came and even if the product clearly carried on past it. m1 shows the rule FAILing a request that ran to completion: both the refused and the delivered sends were recorded, and only then was the 504 faked. On the shared stack, POST /folder-access has already used the whole 60 s before reaching the send. So a refusal reached at about 59 s and then cut off reads as a product FAIL, which the plan forbids for a broken precondition. Judge it INCONCLUSIVE in either of two cases: the product demonstrably got past the refusal (for /access, okDoc's send recorded after it, or the '[email] send failed' line already logged), or the refusal came within a few seconds of the cut-off. FAIL only when the refusal left ample time and nothing followed it.
observations.evidence: e2e/specs/functional/a23-email.spec.mjs:737-745 (`if (before.length === 0)` is the only INCONCLUSIVE branch). The mutant scratchpad/w1a-a23-email-adopt/mutants/m1-refused-then-no-answer.spec.mjs:785 awaits the real access() and then returns a 504; the FAIL is at e2e/.out/2610120656-vuxx/scratch/20261012T140153Z-p85979-rim0. Shared stack e2e/.out/2610102144-wr3h/invocations/20261012T135649Z-p74441-28ue/results.json, A23.6: 'POST /folder-access: no answer after 60 s … the shim saw it not at all yet'. Plan, 'Telling harness bugs from product defects' rule 2.

observations.detail: The 'violates' text of X-a23-email-1 cites 'SPEC §6 concedes only that someone removed from a document keeps, for up to a day, the images their own browser already held (spec.md:1736-1739)'. Those lines are in §17 (Visibility … → Caching), with the same point in §2 GET /thumb (spec.md:264-266). §6 is Annotation mechanics and says nothing of the kind. Fix the section number. Also cite the threat model's asset table, which states the protection the leak breaks. It reads 'Document bytes … owner + members' and 'annotations, comments … anyone with an account who can read the document'. On that basis this is more than a bare SPEC question: the leaked notice carries the anchored passage (document text) and later comments to someone who gets 404 from GET /content.

observations.detail: ringProblem() returns null for any IFRAME stop. A24.2b and A24.2c Tab into the document frame (A24.2h too), and that stop is never judged for a ring. Recorded evidence shows the frame focused by Tab with :focus-visible false and outline-style none, so a keyboard user sees nothing focused. That breaks SPEC §7's "visible :focus-visible" and the test cannot see it. Fix: judge the frame stop (a ring on the iframe, or on a wrapper through :focus-within). Because it is red today, file it as a defect candidate with a TODO case.

observations.detail: The 'never scroll sideways' oracle reads only the page's own scroll width (and scrollX, which never moves on the touch device). The 2 dialogs sit in a position:fixed backdrop, and a fixed box never adds to the page's scroll width. .modal-body is overflow-y:auto, which makes it a sideways scroller too, and so is .viewer-toolbar (overflow-x:auto with the scrollbar hidden), so a too-wide dialog body or toolbar is never seen. The `overflowing` list does catch such boxes, but nothing asserts on it. The placement check is weak the same way: scrollIntoViewIfNeeded scrolls that toolbar or dialog body sideways, so an Edit, Share, Present or Add past the right edge counts as inside. `belowTheFold` is recorded but never judged. Fix: assert scrollWidth <= clientWidth for every scroll container and fixed overlay on each surface (or assert `overflowing` is empty). Judge each primary action's horizontal position as it was at load, and allow only vertical scrolling to reach it. Add a control that widens .viewer-toolbar or .modal-body content.
observations.evidence: spec :589 (sideways uses only scrollWidth/scrolledX), :451-457 (overflowing collected, unjudged), :527-529 (scrollIntoViewIfNeeded before placement), :593 (belowTheFold unused); app/src/styles/dialogs.css:5-6 (.modal-backdrop position:fixed), :35 (.modal-body overflow-y:auto); viewer.css:47-57 (.viewer-toolbar overflow-x:auto; scrollbar-width:none)

observations.detail: The skip reason ('the dependency budget forbids adding it') does not hold. CLAUDE.md's budget covers runtime dependencies of app/ and functions/ only, and the suite already added playwright-core as a root devDependency. What actually blocks axe-core is check:licenses: axe-core is MPL-2.0, which is not on the ALLOWED list. The documented way past that is an EXCEPTIONS entry with a reason, as caniuse-lite has, and that needs the user's decision. The skip should give that reason, and the question should go to the user (an I-class ask), rather than be closed as impossible.

observations.detail: With axe skipped, nothing in the suite checks SPEC §7's 'WCAG AA contrast'. axe's colour-contrast rule is one of the 'serious' issues the catalogue names. Contrast can be checked without any dependency on the 13 surfaces A24.1 already visits: compare each text element's colour with its resolved background, 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large. The other critical axe rules most likely to regress can also be checked: every button and link has an accessible name, every input has a label, and every image has alt text (getByRole or ariaSnapshot).

observations.detail: In forced colours the case reads only the dot's computed border-radius and transform. Those hold whether or not the dot is drawn. The dot is painted only by `background: currentColor`, with no border and no forced-color-adjust, and forced colours replace a background with Canvas. So the shape the case calls 'shown' may be invisible against the Canvas-coloured chip. (Line 1450 compares the chip's text colour, which forced colours make equal anyway.) Fix: under forced colours, assert that the dot's computed background-color, or its border, differs from the chip's background-color in both modes.

observations.detail: spokenText() drops only aria-hidden nodes. It still counts text that is display:none, visibility:hidden or [hidden], which no screen reader reads. The usual regression is the .visually-hidden 'Replace' and 'with' turning into display:none or the hidden attribute. That would still pass both spokenText, because the words are counted, and seenText, because the eye does not see them, while the screen reader says nothing. Fix: skip display:none, visibility:hidden and [hidden] in spokenText, or assert on the ariaSnapshot the case already records.
observations.evidence: spec :1459-1468 (walk skips only aria-hidden), :1504 (ariaSnapshot recorded, never asserted); app/src/annotation/Sidebar.tsx:73-87 (words in span.visually-hidden)

observations.detail: A24.4a opens the comments panel itself before tapping, so 'tapping a highlight opens its thread' is never measured with the panel closed on two columns. SPEC §6's panel-default rule ('nothing after it changes the answer') may say a highlight tap must NOT reopen a panel the reader closed. That makes this a SPEC question to put to the user (I-class) before a case is written, not something to decide in the test.

observations.detail: The ring oracle cites SPEC §10, but it checks only one direction: the ring is drawn in --color-focus. SPEC §10's sentence is that --color-focus appears nowhere but :focus-visible, so that the ring is the only colour of its kind. A link, badge or border drawn in the same colour would leave the ring ambiguous and still pass. Fix: on the A24.1 surfaces, with nothing focused, assert that no element's computed color, background-color, border-color or outline-color equals the resolved --color-focus.

observations.detail: sendRow judges a refused cell by its status, plus the 409 message and the byte parity of a 404/401 with an absent id. It never checks that the refused write left nothing behind. A product that applied the rename (c13), move (c14), /trust (c15t), /marking (c15m), POST /draft (c9), /thumb (c16) or /commit (c11), and then answered 403, 404 or 409, would pass. The sibling a02-matrix-data spec asserts "nothing stored" for every refusal. Fix: snapshot docs/{id} (title, folderId, trusted, marking, thumb, draft, currentVersion) and the draft object before each refused cell, and assert they are unchanged after it.

observations.detail: These cases are tagged BOTH (local and prod), but they cannot pass on production. member() at a02-matrix-http.spec.mjs:432 runs precondition(granted.status === 200 && granted.members?.includes(acct.email)). On production, lib/grant.mjs share() goes through the operator script (via:"operator") and returns json {stdout, stderr}, so granted.members is always undefined. Every case built on member() therefore fails at a precondition whatever the product does. Fix: read docs/{id}.members through readDoc, or check g.mirror, or check only the status when the target is not local.

These four are the merged-view latest on 0a2t, and they are FAILs with no classification. All come from invocation 20261012T050043Z-p19341-9vq2, which is after the spec's mtime. The errors are 'timeout after 60000 ms' and 'owner: a loaded document frame not reached within 60000 ms'. The unit's open_issues calls this saturation (E), but no `classify --merge` was ever run. The cause sits in the spec: a09-editing.spec.mjs uses none of the lib's judges (no inconclusiveOnStackTimeout, inconclusiveOnPageStall or answered()), so every shared-stack non-answer is a FAIL, never INCONCLUSIVE. Fix: classify the four as E citing the 380% Firestore CPU evidence, and adopt the lib stall wiring as a07, a08 and a13 did.

The Done path of X-a09-editing-1 is no longer observed anywhere. The earlier spec had 'A9.6 a Done save that outlasts the debounce is not followed by a second POST /draft of the same edit'. It held Done's POST 1.5 s and asserted exactly one POST. It was todo(failed) in 5 runs on 0a2t (20261011T054918Z … 20261011T060953Z-p5285-9hbp), then dropped in the restructure. The current A9.6 half 2 calls posts.stop() as soon as the toolbar detaches (a09-editing.spec.mjs:546-548), with no QUIET_MS watch. The mechanism still stands: useInlineEditor.ts clears the debounce timer only in the edit-mode cleanup (line 152). That cleanup runs after Done's flush resolves, so a slow Done save lets the timer post the edit again. Plan 9.2 says one POST per pause. Fix: restore the held-Done defect case, or watch QUIET_MS after Done and assert exactly one POST carrying the token.

All three are the latest in wr3h's merged view and are unclassified FAILs on current bytes. A12.3 failed in 20261012T111515Z-p84188-6739 ('pinned: a loaded document frame … /v2/ not reached within 30000 ms') and in 20261012T113350Z-p19577-rnvf ('timeout after 60000 ms'). A12.5 timed out in rnvf. The unit's description of A12.4 does not match its own evidence. The unit calls it an autosave POST /draft that went unanswered. The error says no POST /draft STARTED within 20 s after the last edit, while the save state read 'saving'. In requests-owner.jsonl, a 22.5 s POST /draft is followed by the draft frame reloading twice (GET /draft/…?r=0 at +445.8 s and +445.96 s), about 0.3 s before that edit. That is the same 'saving, nothing sent' signature as smoke's live-edit failures. Fix: triage A12.4 per plan rule 3 before calling it E (rerun on a fresh stack with POST /draft delayed about 20 s through User.delayRequests). Classify A12.3 and A12.5. The a12 spec has no lib stall wiring.

Only three a12 families have a control seen red: controls-version-banner (12.3), controls-update-refusal-bytes (12.5) and controls-delete-version-refusal (12.7). Two others have none, and w1a-a12-versions/mut holds only the a12-public-resync positive. The first is A12.6's stale-base refusal on /publish?update=, update_document, /draft and /commit, with threadsLeftBehind. The plan itself names 'the STALE check removed' as a control. The second is A12.4's dedup of an earlier version's bytes (the S13 assertion: deduped, nothing minted, draft cleared). Fix: add a spec mutation or patch for each, for example drop saveDraft's baseVersion check, or make commit dedup compare against currentVersion only.

It is declared { tiers: ["local"], defect: "X-a12-versions-2" } with no needs and no stated reason (a12-versions.spec.mjs:705). Everything it does is prod-safe: POST /draft, POST /commit, GET /draft, plus Admin readDoc and listObjects. Plan A12 is BOTH, with only 12.7 LOCAL. This is a race whose fix will need a production re-check, so it should be BOTH. If the interval-0 Storage polling is the concern, give it a polling interval and say so.

Five cases end the wr3h merged view as unclassified FAILs on current bytes, all from 20261012T064427Z-p52195-bixh:
- A21.3 and A21.6: 'POST …/access: expected 200, got 504'.
- A21.5: 'MCP tools/call: HTTP 504'.
- A21.5b: a precondition failure, because A21.5 staged nothing.
- A21.7: 'docs/…/events … thread.opened 82 of 103 within 480000 ms'.
A21.1 and A21.2 are flaky: an unclassified FAIL in 20261012T062903Z-p72280-45d7 (504s), then a PASS. The unit's open_issues blames emulator load, and for A21.7 the emulator dropping timed-out trigger runs, but nothing is classified. a21-changes.spec.mjs has no lib judges (0 inconclusiveOn* or answered()), so each Hosting cut-off is a FAIL. Fix: classify these, citing emulators.log's 'Your function timed out' lines for A21.7. Wire cutoffError and inconclusiveOnStackTimeout. Consider giving A21.5b its own staged document so it stops failing whenever A21.5 does.

observations.ref: smoke: owner and editor live-edit … Save as new version (and its BODYATTR follower)
observations.detail: Both cases have FAILed in every wr3h invocation since 20261011T111334Z, 17 in a row up to 20261012T163042Z-p28576-fwbz, and none is classified; they pass on 0a2t. The error is 'both editors settled not met within 20000 ms … save states ["saving","saved"]' (smoke.spec.mjs:177-181). The BODYATTR case then fails its precondition. In fwbz the editor's POST /draft took 19,239 ms, and the owner sent no POST /draft at all while showing 'saving'. A12.4 rnvf shows the same signature. Fix: triage it (product stall or a 20 s settle shorter than the stack's save latency), then classify, or wire smoke to the lib's stall judges.

observations.ref: smoke: owner and viewer sign in … the viewer comments … the owner sees the thread
observations.detail: It flips between PASS and FAIL on current bytes on wr3h, with at least 13 unclassified FAILs (for example 20261011T123220Z-p5234-70cz). Each one is 'Expected … [] vs [{authorEmail, body}]'. The cause is a harness race. smoke.spec.mjs:108-109 reads the annotation's comments collection once, right after the annotation exists. The app writes the annotation (DocViewer.tsx:475 createAnnotation) and the comment (Sidebar.tsx:206 addComment) as separate writes, so on a slow stack the comment is not stored yet. Fix: wrap the comments read in eventually(), and classify the past FAILs H.

The unit's own open_issues says only search-quiet, trusted-deck backfill, expired placeholder and the editor's expired cover POST count were seen red. It names the families never controlled: sort order (updatedAt desc and the createdAt fallback), folder deep links, id rules (400 for a bad id, nothing stored; a taken id becomes {id}-[a-z0-9]{6}), title derivation (<title>, then og:title, then the file name, and a Markdown H1), the folder-delete lift, and members on move. 'Their asserts did fail during development' is not a recorded control. Fix: add spec mutations, for example expect createdAt order, drop the suffix regex anchor, swap title sources, or skip the move.

The unit has 3 product controls: fork-intent (15.1), forks-rules (15.2's forks/* read) and lineage-owner-email (15.3). Its open_issues lists families with no control. There is no spec-mutation dir at all (w1a-a15-forks has none):
- A15.2: stats.forks +1 exactly with other stats untouched; default marking.
- A15.3: the hiddenAncestor walk-stop and the `changed` flag.
- A15.3b: key scope.
- A15.4 and A15.4b: folder refusals (403 or 404, nothing written).
- A15.4d: the version pointer.
Fix: add spec mutations seen red for each.

A16.5 is the plan's 16.5: POST /thumb refuses r≠THUMB_REVISION or a non-current version (409), and a non-JPEG, 160 KiB+1, 1281 px or 101 slides (400), writing nothing, while 160 KiB, 1280×720 and exactly 100 slides are stored. It has no control or mutation; w1a-a16-decks/mut2 holds only m1-tall-is-a-deck and m2-member-as-stranger. A16.1's overview half (o and O toggle; Escape closes only the overview, not defaultPrevented when the overview is shut) has no control either. Fix: add, for example, a mutant that expects a 101-slide upload stored or 1281 px accepted, and one that expects Escape to also end Present.

The a17 controls are print-scrub (17.1), stamp-lock (17.2) and file-print (17.6), plus the menu and recover mutants (classification only) and the shared rehash and decor sets. Two families were never seen red. A17.3 is the PNG at 1×, 2× and 3× equal to border box × scale, plus the diagram PNG and the SVG plus label. A17.5 is POST /marking 200/403/404/401 with refusals changing nothing, the owner-only menu entry, docs/{id}.marking unwritable by clients, and the Account default seeding the dialog and upload. Fix: add mutants, for example expect scale 2 at 3×, expect the editor's 403 as 200, or upload with the default unchecked.

The a19 controls cover A19.1 (notify-optout), A19.2 (analytics-emulators, plus the manual consent-memo-bug patch) and A19.5 (token-shown-once, m1-no-consent). Three families have no control seen red:
- A19.3: the account default marking seeds new documents only (the plain case).
- A19.4: teams create, rename, admin toggle and what it allows, remove and delete, each reporting a count.
- A19.6: each skill zip is application/zip, an attachment, holding exactly <n>/ and <n>/SKILL.md, byte-equal to the served file.
Fix: add mutations or patches for each.

The plan names these CLI oracles explicitly, and none has been seen red:
- A20.7i: suggest needs exactly one of --with and --delete.
- A20.7j: changes --wait --timeout exits 3 with the cursor.
- A20.7k: mv needs its destination, spelled `root`.
- A20.7p: logout revokes its own token (401 after), and revoking another token's id is 403.
The a20-cli controls cover only 7f (zip-route), 7s (watch-debounce), 7u (cli-origin), 7m (ad hoc skill-name) and the json positives. 7c (list paging) and 7d (get past 200k) are also uncontrolled. observations.ref: A20.1, A20.2 (get_document, list_documents, publish_document, move_document), A20.3, A20.4
observations.detail:
a20-mcp's own controls target only A20.5 (channel), A20.2.get_comments (comment-cut) and A20.6 (linkkey). The 'existing sets' it leans on (controls-mcp-tools, a2-mcp-messages, a2-refusal, cache-headers) target smoke, a02-matrix-http and a03, and were never run against this spec. So none of these has been seen red here:
- A20.1: exact tool names.
- A20.2: get_document's 200k cut, list cursor paging, idTaken suffixing, move with no folder going to the root.
- A20.3: missing-argument naming, -32601, -32600, -32700, batch order.
- A20.4: the Bearer challenge text, invalid_token, private no-store plus Expose-Headers on every answer, 405 for GET and DELETE, Allow on PUT.
Fix: run controls-mcp-tools against A20.1, and add mutations for the rest, for example drop WWW-Authenticate from Access-Control-Expose-Headers, or off-by-one the 200k cut.

The controls cover A23.4 (cooldown), A23.2 (recipients, plaintext) and A23.7 (email-off). The m1–m4 mutants test only how cut-offs and extra mail are judged. Four oracle families have no control seen red:
- A23.1: one invitation per new member per kind; a re-grant or role change sends nothing.
- A23.3: a suggestion notice goes to the owner plus approvers, minus the author.
- A23.5: decisions are mailed through the comment branch.
- A23.6: /access, /folder-access and /team-members still answer 200 when the shim returns 500.
Fix: add mutants or patches, for example make setAccess rethrow the send error, mail editors on a suggestion, or invite on every re-grant.

A24.4a is the touch tablet case: a tap on a highlight selects its thread, and a 1.2 s long-press selection shows the action button. A24.5a is mode shown by shape under forced colours. Neither appears among the a24 controls: overflow, reduced-motion, focus-ring, m1-words and m2-trap, plus the a24-fixes positives for the six defect cases. Fix: add spec mutations, for example tap outside the highlight, or compare an editor's chip with an editor's.

Plan 24.5's 'axe reports 0 serious or critical issues' has no executing scenario. A24.5c is declared needs: ["axe-core, not a dependency"], so it is SKIP on every target, permanently. axe-core is not installed anywhere, and the campaign forbids new dependencies, so the reason is true but nothing covers the oracle. The unit's open_issues records this, but not as a plan_oracle_correction for the orchestrator to approve. Fix: either write a dependency-free check of the serious/critical rules that matter on the 11 screens (accessible names for buttons and links, form-label association, img alt, valid ARIA attributes and roles, duplicate ids), or file a plan_oracle_correction citing the dependency budget so G1 can accept the hole.

Plan 3.1 says 'every response carries nosniff'. The header matrix asserts x-content-type-options only on /content, /thumb and the owner's /draft. The /download, /unlock, GET /access and /draft stranger and anonymous rows (a03-visibility.spec.mjs, rows after '/draft (owner)') expect cache-control alone. The product sends no nosniff on /download: downloadBundle sets only Content-Type, Cache-Control and Content-Disposition (functions/src/index.ts:727-731), and firebase.json's /download/** rule adds only Cache-Control. So the plan's assertion would go red there. No plan_oracle_correction records the narrowing (SPEC §2 names nosniff for /content at spec.md:227 and /d at :278). Fix: assert it and record the finding, or file the correction with that citation.

A1.9b is LOCAL only because its framing half needs a spare port. Its header half is a plain anonymous GET of /SIGNUP, /Signup, /CONNECT and /Connect, checking X-Frame-Options and frame-ancestors, and that is prod-safe. CLAUDE.md says response headers are invisible locally and need a real deployment. Production Hosting's case-sensitivity for the /signup and /connect header sources is exactly what the emulator cannot show. Fix: split the HTTP header assertions into a BOTH case, keeping the framing proof LOCAL.

The X-a01-identity-1 oracle (Create account enables within 15 s for a policy-satisfying password) has no positive control showing it can pass, unlike the other a01 defect cases. A1.8b has m8-a18b-short-hold-passes, and A1.9b has the canonical /signup framing precondition. Without one, the TODO could be the oracle's own fault, not the product's. Fix: add a scratch mutant that fulfils the page's /passwordPolicy request with a valid policy via page.route and see 'passed unexpectedly'. That also helps decide whether the 501 is emulator-only (E) or a product robustness defect.

citations.detail: X-a18-stats-1 is presented as a SPEC violation, but the cited SPEC text does not say what the report claims. SPEC §4 says stats exists 'so ... any member can see the AGGREGATE'. That states a purpose. It does not say stats may hold only aggregates. The same section makes app/src/types.ts 'the typed source of truth', and ViewStats declares lastViewedByEmail?: string. SPEC §17 also endorses the same per-person shape on the same member-readable map: lastEditedByEmail 'is now the whole of the answer'. SPEC §17's 'Gated to isDocEditor' covers the activity panel, not docs/{id}. Under the plan's verdict codes this is a Q (SPEC question: report and ask), not a confirmed defect. Fix: retag it as a SPEC question for the user, and put types.ts:155 and the lastEditedByEmail precedent in its 'violates' text. Until the user rules, do not present it as a confirmed defect.
citations.evidence: spec.md:459-460 ('app/src/types.ts is the typed source of truth; this section is normative about meaning'); spec.md:554-556; spec.md:1863-1866 (lastEditedByEmail); spec.md:1877-1881 (activity panel); app/src/types.ts:155; a18-stats.spec.mjs:546,569

citations.detail: X-a16-decks-1's `violates` field cites SPEC §6d, but that sentence describes what the product does. SPEC says a stacked deck 'reads position from which slide is *shown* … with the deck's own attribute changes as the signal'. useDeck measures shownSlide on exactly that signal, a MutationObserver on class/style (useDeck.ts:174-188). At that moment the outgoing slide is the one shown by SPEC's own four properties. SPEC names no later signal, such as transitionend. So the defect stands on its concrete harm (every other ArrowRight is lost, and the rail marks the wrong slide on the repo's own sample), not on a broken SPEC sentence. Re-tag it as class I, or as P on concrete harm with a SPEC question attached. Its fix (for example, re-measuring after transitions, or not letting a mutation overwrite goTo's setCurrent) changes normative text, so it waits at G1. The failing assertion itself is correct: it is the defect's own oracle (:599), with the no-transitions twin as its precondition.
citations.evidence: SPEC spec.md:875-879; app/src/viewer/useDeck.ts:174-188, :237-238; app/src/viewer/deck.ts isShown/shownIndex; report product_suspicions X-a16-decks-1 'violates'; e2e/specs/functional/a16-decks.spec.mjs:594-599

citations.detail: The report says S15 violates SPEC, but neither citation supports that. It rests on ADR 0014 ('limits a disabled account's remaining access to about an hour') and on SPEC §23's 'not disabled' check at refresh, and both cover OAuth grants (bsa_/bsr_) only. For personal tokens ADR 0014 Decision 3 says the opposite: 'The identity gate is re-checked at each refresh, which a personal token never gets.' SPEC §19's 'same identity, and therefore the same ACL' is about the ACL, not account state. So the behaviour S15 shows is documented: an I-class finding to ask about (the plan tags it Q), not a violation. The failing assertion is the right one; the classification and citation are wrong. Fix: rewrite product_suspicions.S15.violates and the spec header to cite ADR 0014:25-27 as acknowledging the behaviour, present 401 as the proposed answer to the question, and classify it I.
citations.evidence: docs/architecture/adr/0014-oauth-for-the-agent-surface.md:25-27 and :52 (the hour is the OAuth access token's); docs/architecture/threat-model.md:382 (OAuth section); spec.md:2753 (§23 refresh re-check list); a19-account.spec.mjs:37-41 and :809-811; plan S15 row 'Q (security)'; report product_suspicions[S15].violates

citations.detail: All three defects cite only spec.md:2206, 'Every command takes `--json`'. Literally, that says the flag is accepted, and open, login --paste and publish --watch all accept it and exit 0. It does not say stdout must be exactly one JSON value, so a skeptic can call these intended behaviour or a SPEC question. Stronger sources: spec.md:2233-2235 ('says so on stderr, which keeps `--json` output parseable'), which is about `publish` and so applies directly to X-a20-cli-3; the CLI's own usage line cli/src/index.mjs:110 '--json machine-readable output'; and the login comment at :197. Re-cite with these. For X-a20-cli-1/2, rest the P on the concrete harm, or tag them Q per the plan's verdict codes.

X-a14-workspace-1's `violates` field cites SPEC §2, and the case name says "(SPEC §2)". That sentence only sets the server's default when `title` is absent. The drop path sends an explicit title. The server honours it, as §2 and A14.3's own "a typed title wins" require, so nothing the server does breaks §2, and §2 says nothing about what a client must send. citations.detail: The S8 citation does not say what the report claims. SPEC §6b (spec.md:774-791) says nothing about the live log, and ADR 0010 never says the log wins over the draft. The normative sentence is in §22, spec.md:2531-2533: "Because the live log wins over the draft when an editor opens (§6b) … a log nobody is using is dropped with the write". ADR 0015 point 4 says the same. presence.ts:141 repeats the same wrong §6b reference. The concrete harm cited ("a v3 published from bytes after the commit … showed v2's text") is S8 combined with S6/S14: no path that publishes from bytes clears status/{doc}/y, because clearEditLog is called only from accept.ts. After an in-app commit on its own, the surviving log is the draft that just became v2, so an editor who adopts it sees v2. Either fix alone removes the cited harm: S8's, or the S14+S6 direction "every mint path … clears the live log", which the plan runs before S8. Fix: cite §22 (spec.md:2531-2533) and the intent at DocViewer.tsx:563-567. Then show a harm S8 causes on its own, or say plainly that the harm depends on S6/S14, so the fix order is judged on the right evidence. The oracle itself, y empty within 2 s of the toast, is fine.

citations.detail: `early` is read as soon as the workspace card shows. The card comes from the docs listener, but the account record comes from a separate listener (watchUser), so nothing guarantees the record had arrived at the moment of the read. Only the later `fresh` loop shows that it arrived, and the evidence does not record when. Today the dialog reads the default only at mount, so `early` is false either way. The red is therefore not shown to be X-a17-export-6's own oracle, and after a fix the same read could still be false on a slow stack. Fix: after the card shows, poll the still-open early dialog's box inside ctx.oracle(() => eventually(...)) with a bounded timeout, then run the fresh-dialog check as the precondition that proves the record arrived, and write both timings to seed.json.

citations.detail: X-a17-export-1 cites ADR 0007 / CLAUDE.md #3, 'decoration must never reach serialized bytes'. Those passages are about serializeCleanHtml and the bytes saved from the editor, not about an image export. SPEC §20 says the browser's File→Print 'prints what is on screen, highlights included', which a skeptic will use to argue that highlights in an exported PNG are intended. Cite the SPEC sentences that do support the claim: §6 'Highlights are presentational and are NEVER persisted' (a downloaded SVG carrying data-bshd-ann ids and bshd-hl wrappers persists them) and the preview rule that one reader's annotations never appear. Consider splitting the claim: the SVG file as P, and the PNG's pixels as class I (report and ask).

This one is latent. In a `defect:` case, any plain assert that fails is booked as that defect's TODO. Line 672 is a setup step written as an assert (POST /marking stores the marking), and lines 682-683 check the link holder's sandbox and scrub. Neither is X-a17-export-4's oracle. If POST /marking, the sandbox or the scrub regressed for link holders, the case would stay TODO under X-a17-export-4 instead of FAILing. Fix: make line 672 a precondition. Make 682-683 preconditions too, or move those checks into a non-defect case. Add a positive control inside the case (the owner prints this same document and gets both stamps) rather than relying on A17.1.

citations.detail: A collapsed caret broadcasts no focus, so peers never see another editor's caret. The report calls this 'Class I, recorded and not asserted'. Class I means the behaviour matches the SPEC but may be harmful. Here the product contradicts SPEC §16 in five sentences: 'the live caret', 'carets carry name labels', 'per-peer caret bars', 'focus — selection or caret', and 'Peer carets and selections update at 200 ms'. The only counterweight is an implementation note naming describeAnchorFromSelection. The caret check did fail: on stack 0a2t, A11.2 and A11.3 failed with 'carets 0'. Both cases were then rewritten to use a drag selection (selectIn), and their names still say 'caret'. The report records 1 repro run, but the 0a2t failures are two more. Fix: add a defect-tagged case (X-a11-live-1). In it, a real click places a collapsed caret, and the oracle requires peers/{uid}/focus to be non-null and a reader's #bshd-peers to draw a labelled .bshd-peer-caret. Alternatively, raise it explicitly as Q at G1 instead of a recorded note.

citations.detail: The mechanism in the report says 'materialise drops INJECTED_ATTRS (sync.ts:43, :156)'. That is wrong. materialise (sync.ts:61-80) copies every attribute it receives from the wire. sync.ts:156 and :221 are in toY (DOM to CRDT), and binding.ts:108 drops the attribute at seed time. Keeping data-bshd-empty off the wire is correct (ADR 0010). The defect is that nothing re-runs markGeneratedContainers after the adopt branch's host.replaceChildren (sync.ts:272-281). As written, the text invites a 'fix' that puts the decoration on the wire, and the previous gap shows the suite would accept such a fix. Correct the mechanism to say 'joiner never re-marks after adopt' and cite useInlineEditor.ts:136 together with sync.ts:272-281.

citations.detail: The 'violates' field cites SPEC §2 'POST /draft, GET /draft/** … Editor-gated'. That sentence gates the HTTP draft endpoints, not reads of RTDB status/{doc}/y. SPEC §16 gates only writes to the shared log ('Writes to the shared log are gated by editAccess') and says nothing about reads. The DENY oracle therefore rests on the plan (A2 c18 V) and on the harm (a viewer decodes an editor's unsaved keystrokes). The rules file's own principle supports it: database.rules.json:43, 'document state is gated on "may edit"'. The defect stands on that harm. Restate 'violates' as harm plus the rules principle, by analogy with §2, and note that the fix must add a SPEC §16 sentence on reads. As written, it presents a SPEC-silent change as 'restoring' SPEC, which matters for the plan's 'Ask? no' at G1.

On that basis this is more than a bare SPEC question: the leaked notice carries the anchored passage (document text) and later comments to someone who gets 404 from GET /content.

citations.detail: Plan 3.1 says 'every response carries nosniff'. The header matrix asserts x-content-type-options only on /content, /thumb and the owner's /draft. The /download, /unlock, GET /access and /draft stranger and anonymous rows (a03-visibility.spec.mjs, rows after '/draft (owner)') expect cache-control alone. The product sends no nosniff on /download: downloadBundle sets only Content-Type, Cache-Control and Content-Disposition (functions/src/index.ts:727-731), and firebase.json's /download/** rule adds only Cache-Control. So the plan's assertion would go red there. No plan_oracle_correction records the narrowing (SPEC §2 names nosniff for /content at spec.md:227 and /d at :278). Fix: assert it and record the finding, or file the correction with that citation.

a09-editing.detail: These four are the merged-view latest on 0a2t, and they are FAILs with no classification. All come from invocation 20261012T050043Z-p19341-9vq2, which is after the spec's mtime. The errors are 'timeout after 60000 ms' and 'owner: a loaded document frame not reached within 60000 ms'. The unit's open_issues calls this saturation (E), but no `classify --merge` was ever run. The cause sits in the spec: a09-editing.spec.mjs uses none of the lib's judges (no inconclusiveOnStackTimeout, inconclusiveOnPageStall or answered()), so every shared-stack non-answer is a FAIL, never INCONCLUSIVE. Fix: classify the four as E citing the 380% Firestore CPU evidence, and adopt the lib stall wiring as a07, a08 and a13 did.

The Done path of X-a09-editing-1 is no longer observed anywhere. The earlier spec had 'A9.6 a Done save that outlasts the debounce is not followed by a second POST /draft of the same edit'. It held Done's POST 1.5 s and asserted exactly one POST. It was todo(failed) in 5 runs on 0a2t (20261011T054918Z … 20261011T060953Z-p5285-9hbp), then dropped in the restructure. The current A9.6 half 2 calls posts.stop() as soon as the toolbar detaches (a09-editing.spec.mjs:546-548), with no QUIET_MS watch. The mechanism still stands: useInlineEditor.ts clears the debounce timer only in the edit-mode cleanup (line 152). That cleanup runs after Done's flush resolves, so a slow Done save lets the timer post the edit again. Plan 9.2 says one POST per pause. Fix: restore the held-Done defect case, or watch QUIET_MS after Done and assert exactly one POST carrying the token.

a12-versions.detail: All three are the latest in wr3h's merged view and are unclassified FAILs on current bytes. A12.3 failed in 20261012T111515Z-p84188-6739 ('pinned: a loaded document frame … /v2/ not reached within 30000 ms') and in 20261012T113350Z-p19577-rnvf ('timeout after 60000 ms'). The error says no POST /draft STARTED within 20 s after the last edit, while the save state read 'saving'. In requests-owner.jsonl, a 22.5 s POST /draft is followed by the draft frame reloading twice (GET /draft/…?r=0 at +445.8 s and +445.96 s), about 0.3 s before that edit. a01-identity.detail: A1.9b is LOCAL only because its framing half needs a spare port. Its header half is a plain anonymous GET of /SIGNUP, /Signup, /CONNECT and /Connect, checking X-Frame-Options and frame-ancestors, and that is prod-safe. CLAUDE.md says response headers are invisible locally and need a real deployment. Production Hosting's case-sensitivity for the /signup and /connect header sources is exactly what the emulator cannot show. Fix: split the HTTP header assertions into a BOTH case, keeping the framing proof LOCAL.

The X-a01-identity-1 oracle (Create account enables within 15 s for a policy-satisfying password) has no positive control showing it can pass, unlike the other a01 defect cases. A1.8b has m8-a18b-short-hold-passes, and A1.9b has the canonical /signup framing precondition. Without one, the TODO could be the oracle's own fault, not the product's. Fix: add a scratch mutant that fulfils the page's /passwordPolicy request with a valid policy via page.route and see 'passed unexpectedly'. That also helps decide whether the 501 is emulator-only (E) or a product robustness defect.

An Auth emulator that stalled for more than 15 s would therefore FAIL the case (eventually timeout outside ctx.oracle) instead of making it INCONCLUSIVE. I have never seen this: 44 earlier runs plus these 3 were all TODO. I did not change it, because that is outside the interrupted edit.

(/unlock), spec.md:326-327 "`Cache-Control: private, no-store` on every answer, the refusals included." citations.note: Mechanism: downloadBundle sets Content-Type, Cache-Control and Content-Disposition only (functions/src/index.ts:727-731). noStore() sets Cache-Control only (functions/src/lib/http.ts:74-76). firebase.json's /download/** rule adds Cache-Control only (firebase.json:66-67), and no header rule covers /unlock or /access. Observed in all 3 runs: all 8 answers had nosniff null. The zips were application/zip; the /unlock and /access 200s were application/json; the 404s and the 401 had no content type and an empty body. No concrete harm: a browser does not sniff a declared application/zip sent with Content-Disposition: attachment; ORB blocks cross-origin JSON even without the header; the session cookie is SameSite=Strict (functions/src/index.ts:258, :335), so a cross-site page cannot make a member's request at all. The header would be defence in depth only. That makes this class Q, not I and not P. The critic's statement about the /draft stranger and anonymous rows was already out of date: they assert nosniff, and controls-a03-nosniff has been seen red on them.

citations.note: Checked against v0.16.0. (a) Right: §6b (spec.md:790-806) has no live-log text, and ADR 0010 never mentions the log. (ADR 0015 point 4 attributes 'the live log wins over the draft' to ADR 0010, but ADR 0010 does not say it.) (b) Right: the cited harm needed S6/S14. An in-app commit alone leaves the log of the draft that just became v2. The 'v3 from bytes showed v2' harm came from updates that never cleared the log. 0.16.0's commitNewVersion now clears it once the version is current (functions/src/lib/publish.ts:486-488 editorsRefusal, 537-539 and 597-608 dropReplacedDraft with clearEditLog through Admin). So that harm is gone with S8 still present. (c) Partly wrong: the §22 sentence the critic names as normative (spec.md:2556-2559 in 0.16.0, 2531-2533 before) is scoped to an agent's accept ('the write' is the accept's). The new §16 paragraph (spec.md:1556-1563) lists the writes that drop a log nobody is using: writes made outside the editor (accept, commit_draft, every update). The in-app commit is not among them. No SPEC sentence requires the in-app commit to clear the log, so it is not P. The mechanism stands (app DocViewer.tsx:580 clearLog; crdt/rtdb.ts:72 whole-node remove; database.rules.json:98-103 per-entry writes only; rtdb.ts:73-75 swallows the error), and the app's own code means to clear it (DocViewer.tsx:576-579). The harm S8 alone leaves is traced in source and not reproduced. The log holds the published draft plus any keys typed into the session after the pre-commit save. The next opener adopts it over v2's bytes, and their first save makes it a draft of v2. Clearing the log would instead lose a co-editor's late keys. That trade-off is the SPEC question. Edited in the spec: the header item, the case's doc comment and its assertion message. The case name, defect tag and oracle are unchanged. citations.new_citation: S8 is a SPEC QUESTION (class Q), not a violation. The nearest SPEC sentence is §16, spec.md:1556-1560: "The log belongs to the draft. When an editor opens a document, a log that holds anything wins over the bytes it loaded, because it may hold edits they do not. So a write made outside the editor is refused while anybody is in it, and drops a log nobody is using: an agent's accept and `commit_draft` (§22), and every update …". The in-app commit is not on that list. The app's own intent, DocViewer.tsx:576-579, is to clear the log on commit ("Leaving it behind means the next person to open the editor syncs the old draft from the log and it reappears on top of the version that replaced it"), and the realtime rules deny it (database.rules.json:98-103). The harm cited before (a v3 from bytes showed v2's text) needed S6/S14 as well, and 0.16.0 fixed those (publish.ts:537-539, 597-608). What S8 alone leaves is traced in source, not reproduced. The log keeps any keys typed after the pre-commit save. The next person to open the editor on v2 adopts them over v2's bytes and autosaves them as a draft of v2.

The counterweight, spec.md:1521-1523, describes how a SELECTION travels and does not withdraw the caret. A new defect case, A11.2b (defect X-a11-live-1), asserts it. A real mouse click places a collapsed caret in #e2e-8. The oracle requires peers/{uid}/focus to be non-null, and the reader's #bshd-peers to draw a labelled .bshd-peer-caret on #e2e-8. Highlights are presentational and are NEVER persisted.' Nearest: §6:650-651 (a picture is presentation), §20:2364-2365 (highlights accepted on File → Print only), and against it §6d:938-940. citations.new_citation: Replacement 'violates' text: CLASS I, not a SPEC violation. The product does what ADR 0014 documents, and that is arguably harmful. Ask at G1. ADR 0014 Decision 3, docs/architecture/adr/0014-oauth-for-the-agent-surface.md:25-27: "Short-lived and re-checked. An access token lasts an hour and works on `/mcp` only. The refresh token rotates on every use. The identity gate is re-checked at each refresh, which a personal token never gets." SPEC §23 spec.md:2777-2778, "The gate is re-checked at every refresh: - not disabled", and ADR 0014:52-53, "A disabled account keeps up to an hour of access, until its access token expires and the next refresh fails the gate" (also threat-model.md:382-383), are about OAuth grants (bsa_/bsr_) only. The nearest SPEC sentence for a personal token is §19 spec.md:1983-1984: "A token carries the same identity, and therefore the same ACL, as the person who minted it." It concerns the ACL, not the account's state. Mechanism: verifyToken (functions/src/lib/tokens.ts:214-257) reads only the token record and has no expiry check; resolveCaller (functions/src/lib/actor.ts:111-134) accepts the token on every endpoint that takes a bearer; the session goes through verifySessionCookie(cookie, true) (functions/src/lib/auth.ts:97), which refuses a disabled user. Harm: disabling an account is how an operator cuts a person off. It stops their browser at once, but every bsk_ token they minted keeps their whole ACL, with no expiry, until each one is revoked. Revoke is on the person's own account screen, which the disable has just closed, and no operator script revokes one person's tokens. Proposed answer: refuse the token (401) once its owner's Auth user is disabled.

citations.new_citation: SPEC QUESTION (class Q), not a SPEC violation. Nearest SPEC sentence: §19 spec.md:2231 "Every command takes `--json`.", with `open <slug>` among the commands (spec.md:2228). The SPEC never says what open prints under --json. Read literally, 'takes' already holds: the flag is accepted and the command exits 0. Product text against the behaviour, not SPEC: the CLI's usage describes --json as "machine-readable output" (cli/src/index.mjs:110), and the agent guide repeats "Every command takes `--json`." Harm: a caller that appends --json to every command and parses stdout fails on open alone. `bikeshed open <id> --json` prints the bare address ('<external-url><id>\n'), so `| jq` is a parse error. Question for the owner: does 'takes `--json`' mean that every command prints one JSON value under it? Mechanism unchanged: cli/src/index.mjs:1007-1019 (open() never reads flags.json; :1018 console.log(url)).

citations.new_citation: Replacement 'violates' text for X-a23-email-1. Class I: it matches the SPEC and is harmful; report and ask. SPEC §14 spec.md:1372-1373: "recipients = owner + prior thread participants − the author". This names prior participants without exception, and spec.md:1381-1382 has a withdrawal reach "the owner and everybody who has written in the thread". The product follows this literally: functions/src/index.ts:2972-2975 adds every sibling comment's author and never reads doc.members for them. No SPEC sentence excludes a removed participant. The only thing the SPEC lets a removed member keep is in SPEC §17 (Caching), spec.md:1762-1764: "what the window concedes is that someone removed from a document keeps, for up to a day, the images their own browser already held". The same point is in §2 GET /thumb, spec.md:265-266: "the window bounds what a removed member's browser keeps". Those are images the browser already held, never new content. The mail crosses the read boundary the SPEC draws elsewhere: SPEC §4 spec.md:539 "`members` is the EFFECTIVE read set", and SPEC §17 spec.md:1599-1601, where who can read a private document's bytes is "owner + members". The threat model's asset table states the protection, though it is not normative: threat-model.md:9 "Document bytes … owner + `members`" and threat-model.md:11 "Reviewer identities (annotations, comments) … anyone with an account who can read the document". Concrete harm: after POST /access removes the reader, GET /content answers them 404. Yet the next reply's notice mails them up to 300 characters of the anchored passage (index.ts:2979), up to 2000 characters of the new comment (index.ts:2982-2983) and, in the subject, the commenter's address. To be P, §14 would need to add '− anyone who can no longer read the document'. That is a normative change, so it waits for G1.
citations.note: Verified at v0.16.0 (2d545e4). §6 (Annotation mechanics) starts at spec.md:632 and contains no sentence about removal: an awk over 632-992 for remov/member/revok finds only DOM-removal and theme lines. The quoted sentence is spec.md:1759-1764 under '### Caching' (spec.md:1751) in §17 (spec.md:1593). At v0.15.1 it was 1736-1739, so the critic's numbers were right for that tree. The asset-table rows are threat-model.md:9 and :11 now, where the critic had :8 and :11. Why not P: the critic's 'more than a bare SPEC question' holds, because the harm is concrete and the read boundary is SPEC text. But the recipient rule in §14 is explicit, and so is the withdrawal sentence at spec.md:1381-1382, and the product implements both exactly. The read-boundary sentences (§4:539, §17:1599-1601, §17:1694-1698 'Who may read, decided once in lib/acl.ts readBasis') govern reads through the rules and endpoints, not who is mailed. So two SPEC passages pull against each other, and the product sides with the explicit one. That is I by the plan's table: 'matches the SPEC or an ADR but is arguably harmful | report and ask'. The old text 'A SPEC question (I-class)' mixed Q and I; it is I. groups.mechanism_hint: S4: functions/src/lib/draft.ts:276-290 mints v(max+1) and save()s each file with no ifGenerationMatch; STALE is checked only inside the transaction at draft.ts:297. functions/src/lib/publish.ts:495-503 (commitNewVersion) does the same through uploadBundle(storagePrefix, files) with no CREATE_ONLY (compare publish.ts:276 CREATE_ONLY and :374, where v1 uses it); STALE at publish.ts:511, after the upload. groups.mechanism_hint: S2: app/src/crdt/sync.ts:105 applyRemote sets node.data = target.toString(), replacing the whole Text.data under the local caret. S2b: sync.ts:118-139 rebuildChildren ends in node.replaceChildren(...next) on <body>, collapsing a caret anywhere under it when a peer presses Enter. X-c05-structure-3: sync.ts:197-213 diffs a characterData mutation by the LONGEST common prefix, so a letter typed just before the same letter is inserted after the original item (y.insert at :213); a concurrent deletion by item identity then removes the wrong letter. S1: app/src/viewer/useSharedDocument.ts:66-72 connect, await log.ready() (app/src/crdt/rtdb.ts:26-40, first value event), then bindSync; on an empty fragment sync.ts:260-271 seeds via an async append (app/src/crdt/log.ts:108-113), so simultaneous joiners each seed the body. S27: database.rules.json:56 gates status/{d} reads on presenceAccess (members only) while :100 lets editAccess '*' write (functions/src/lib/presence.ts:102 adds '*' to editAccess only); a denied read resolves ready() as empty (rtdb.ts:33-38), so the open-edit non-member seeds a second body; app/src/pages/DocViewer.tsx:308 shareLive admits a public non-member. Skeptic angles: human-paced typing vs scripted bursts (C2 window passes; the damage needs remote patches mid-typing); S1's window is under 100 ms locally and 100-300 ms at 150 ms RTT, so a natural-timing repro matters; fix directions are G1 asks for S2/S2b (delta patching) and S27 (let '*' read y, or stop seeding).

items.claim: A commit that passed POST /commit's base check reads the draft prefix after another mint deleted it. It hashes v1's files alone and answers 200 {versionId: v1, deduped: true}, so the app shows 'No changes to publish' instead of the stale 409. This happens in the in-app race (C8 S4b, where the dedup branch also deletes a draft saved on the new version in that window) and across the two mint paths (C9b S4b: an update_document that passed the editors question mints v2 and drops the draft under an editor's commit already past the base check).

items.claim: Concurrent sharing changes lose grants AND revocations. setAccess, setFolderAccess, recomputeSubtree and refanTeam each read a record and write grant lists or sets computed from that read, with no transaction or precondition. A lost grantee reads 404. A lost REMOVAL puts every revoked editor back in the record: the editor reads the document and is allowed to write the live log. On folders, the lost grantees of a natural race were not even invited.

That matches the 30 s Shutdown of the Database emulator's namespace failure seen in km4o (NPE while flushing a batch, then 'Namespace failure … clearing connections', 'Active to Shutdown', and 30 s later 'Shutdown to Active'). baseline.mechanism: app/src/crdt/sync.ts:197-213. 'Diff by common prefix and suffix' takes the LONGEST common prefix first. When the inserted character equals the character after the caret, the prefix runs across the original character, and y.insert lands one position later, after the original item instead of before it. The text string is the same, but the item identities are swapped. A remote deletion by item identity (Yjs) then removes the wrong one. The serial controls pass because, once the token has reached the deleter, its deletion is again by position in a text that already holds the token.

baseline.violates: Re-cited, after the critic's review. SPEC §6b spec.md:792-794 'their edits merge and every copy converges', and §16 spec.md:1542-1544 'every copy converges on the same document whatever order the updates arrive in': the durable copies, the draft every editor reads (§6a spec.md:751-755) and the version commit_draft mints, do not converge on what every live copy converged to. app/src/crdt/log.ts:16-20 states the design: 'The log is NOT the durable artifact. The draft and the published versions are … it can be … lost entirely without losing a document'. Here dropping the log (spec.md:1556-1559) loses the merged document. Addressing spec.md:748-750, 'Leaving edit mode saves only an edit the autosave has not yet taken. Any save creates a draft, so a save on the way out of an unchanged session would leave a draft that differs from nothing': useInlineEditor.ts:171-173 is a literal reading of 'an edit' as a local one. The sentence's own rationale does not apply, because this session is changed and the draft differs from the merged document. Whether a remote merge counts as 'an edit the autosave has not yet taken' is the G1 question. If it does not, the class is Q, with the concrete harm above. spec.md:804-806 (deletion beats typing) is NOT what is violated: C5 live shows the CRDT semantics hold.
