baseline.mechanism:
Re-checked at HEAD:
- functions/src/index.ts:946 calls parseExpiry(body?.expiresAt).
- functions/src/lib/access.ts:238 maps undefined to {value: null}, the same as an explicit null.
- functions/src/index.ts:963-970 then writes expiresAt: FieldValue.delete().
- index.ts:998-1000 records a doc.expiry event {from: <date>, to: null}.

The members' next autosave (p1's POST /draft 200, 15-20 s after the link holder's, without its token) replaces the draft it saved, because the members' live log never held the edit. baseline.claim: An unlisted link holder's edit is lost without notice. The members' next autosave (p1's POST /draft 200, 15-20 s after the link holder's, without its token) replaces the draft it saved, because the members' live log never held the edit. The link holder is never told; every member is shown the conflict banner.
baseline.mechanism: DocViewer.tsx:308 keeps the link holder out of the live log, as SPEC §16 requires. The members' autosaves then serialize a document without its edit. useLiveSync.ts:44 `if (!meta) return;` and a link holder has no docs/{id} (firestore.rules:147), so the conflict banner of useLiveSync.ts:54-58 never reaches it.
baseline.violates: Weighed against SPEC §16 spec.md:1542-1544, 'Anyone who may edit a document may edit it at any time … edits merge, and every copy converges on the same document whatever order the updates arrive in'. Read alone, that sentence makes this a P: the link holder may edit, its edit does not merge, its copy never converges, and the outcome depends on arrival order. But the same section carves link holders out by name. spec.md:1570-1571 says they 'edit through /draft instead … and are not merged live with the members'. spec.md:1583 lists 'live co-editing through an unlisted link' as deliberately not built. ADR 0012:54-56 calls /draft 'the documented fallback when there is no Realtime Database', which is whole-document last-writer-wins. Whether the carve-out waives 'every copy converges' for link holders (then the loss is intended and only the missing notice is in question) or only the LIVE channel (then the loss is a P, and 'told' is not enough) is a SPEC question, so it stays Q. The judge asserts the weaker reading (kept, or told), which is red under both readings. A P reading would also need 'kept', which C23 told-serial shows the oracle can pass.

baseline.mechanism: verifyToken (functions/src/lib/tokens.ts:214-254) checks only the token record (format, existence, revokedAt, kind, hash) and never reads the Auth user. Sessions go through admin.auth().verifySessionCookie(cookie, true) (functions/src/lib/auth.ts:97), which refuses a disabled user.
baseline.violates: SPEC §19 says a token carries 'the same identity, and therefore the same ACL, as the person who minted it'. SPEC §23 re-checks 'not disabled' at every OAuth refresh, and ADR 0014 limits a disabled account's remaining access to about an hour. A personal token has no such limit. Harm: disabling an account is the operator's way to cut someone off, yet their bsk_ tokens keep working on /mcp indefinitely.

baseline.mechanism: useDeck.ts:184-188 runs measure() (useDeck.ts:174) from a MutationObserver on class/style. The deck toggles .active, so measure runs at the mutation, before the transition. The incoming slide is still at opacity 0, and the outgoing one stays visible for 0.35 s (content/deck-animated/bundle/index.html:113,118). deck.ts:324 counts opacity<=0 as not shown, and deck.ts:333-334 takes the first slide shown, so the result is the outgoing slide. That overwrites goTo's setCurrent(slide.index) (useDeck.ts:237-238). The transition's end mutates no attribute, so current stays stale. The next goTo(current+1) targets the slide already shown and presses nothing.
baseline.violates: SPEC §6d says navigation on a stacked deck 'reads position from which slide is *shown* … with the deck's own attribute changes as the signal'. The signal fires before the slide is shown. Concrete harm: half the reader's ArrowRight presses do nothing, and the rail and overview mark the wrong slide on the repo's own animated sample.

baseline.claim: Once a reader is removed from a document, GET /content answers them 404. Yet they keep getting a comment notice for later replies in any thread they wrote in. Each notice carries the anchored passage (up to 300 characters) and the new comment (up to 2000 characters).
baseline.mechanism: onCommentCreated adds every sibling comment author to the recipients with no membership check (functions/src/index.ts:2972-2975: `for (const c of siblingSnap.docs) { … if (e) recipients.add(e); }`). It then builds the notice from the anchor quote and the comment body (index.ts:2979-2983) and sends it to each recipient who has an account record and whose cooldown allows it. `doc` is already read at index.ts:2962, but its members are never consulted for participants. Fix direction (e2e/patches/a23-fix-removed-participant): mail sibling authors only while they are in doc.members. With it, A23.2b passes and A23.2 still passes.
baseline.violates: A SPEC question (I-class) with concrete harm. SPEC §14's recipient rule is literally 'owner + prior thread participants − the author' and does not exclude removed members. SPEC §6 concedes only that 'someone removed from a document keeps, for up to a day, the images their own browser already held' (docs/architecture/spec.md:1736-1739), never new content. So removal (POST /access remove) revokes reading but not the mailing of new document text. It matches none of the plan's suspects S1–S31.

items.claim: The Database emulator's namespace fails under several concurrent writers on one path. For 30 s it answers 503 'Firebase database instance is inactive' to reads and internal_error to in-flight writes, and it clears every connection.

baseline.claim: The Database emulator's namespace fails under several concurrent writers on one path. For 30 s it answers 503 'Firebase database instance is inactive' to reads and internal_error to in-flight writes, and it clears every connection.
baseline.mechanism: From the emulator's own log (logs/database-debug.log). NamespaceActor: 'Encountered unknown exception while flushing batch'. java.lang.NullPointerException: ListBuffer.last0() is null, at scala.collection.mutable.ListBuffer.$plus$eq (ListBuffer.scala:176) <- com.firebase.util.data.RequestContext.addRuleResult (RequestContext.scala:30) <- NamespaceAccessor.canWrite (NamespaceAccessor.scala:103, :78) <- PrefetchQueue.primeWrite (PrefetchQueue.scala:70), run in a scala Future on the akka ForkJoin pool. Concurrent rule evaluations of one batch append to one non-thread-safe ListBuffer. Then: 'Namespace failure for demo-bikeshed; clearing connections', 'status Active to Shutdown', and 30 s later 'Shutdown to Active'. Seen twice this round, in C2 window at N=5 (5 writers to status/{d}/y). Each time it came while the RTDB proxy released the typing's queued appends, 0.4 s (cyam) and 1.9 s (jzpy) after the first queued append was due and before the reset, so lib/proxy.mjs drained() was not involved. The third attempt passed. Load was moderate (1-min 4.4 on 16 CPUs, ~48 GB available, no swap-outs). The harness handles it correctly: settleLive's rtdbGetPatient ends the case INCONCLUSIVE ('the stack did not answer') after 5 s of 503s. Not a product defect, since the product cannot cause an NPE inside the emulator. The client half is X-c01-typing-2.
baseline.evidence: e2e/.out/2610131539-jzpy/logs/database-debug.log (lines 25-99); e2e/.out/2610131550-cyam/logs/database-debug.log (lines 20-94); e2e/.out/2610131539-jzpy/invocations/20261013T224020Z-p35400-5f4e/evidence/c2-window-n-editors-type-tokens-at-the-end-of-one-paragraph-inside-the-rtdb-prox/stack-did-not-answer.txt; e2e/.out/2610131550-cyam/invocations/20261013T225042Z-p96836-9zj5/evidence/c2-window-n-editors-type-tokens-at-the-end-of-one-paragraph-inside-the-rtdb-prox/stack-did-not-answer.txt; first occurrence (cause unrecorded then): e2e/.out/2610130353-9akl
baseline.report: Database emulator (firebase-database-emulator) namespace failure: an NPE in RequestContext.addRuleResult during concurrent rule evaluation, followed by 30 s of Shutdown (503 and internal_error). It recurred in W2 4 times (2610132240-0fzn, 2610140043-xkzg, 2610140131-737w, 2610140353-0q3x) and made 9 trials INCONCLUSIVE (C3 ×4, C12a/b ×2, C22 ×3). Tag it local-only. It is the natural trigger behind X-c01-typing-2 (G06) and the lead for X-c12-agent-vs-editors-2 (G03).
